questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most crucial for me was having interresting and a broad selection of classes. My host university provided a good range of selections of classes. That made it easy for me, in knowing what i had to choose.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Information was good. I had a meeting before my classes started and it helped find my way around campus. The acces to any guidance from the incoming erasmus students was excelent and I always felt heard and taken seriously.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an info meeting, but I had to get to know campus and my classrooms by myself. The Erasmus office at my facualty was indeed very helpfull and good. But still a little bit more guidance or ways to engage in social events would have been nice to know, instead of having to search it on my own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There was the student dorm called villa, which is where the spanish and most erasmus people stayed, then there was also a hotel right next to it that was more expensive. But the dorms were perfect for the price and location.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a grocery store, resturants and other places to get food for a good price. A lot of different options. A cafe too. Kitchen in my own dorm that worked perfectly

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it is very funny and that you can meet a lot of new peopole, experience new events. Having a roomate is fun, and there is good facilities for sports and hangouts.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process was easy and very managable. The explination of the curriculum and the class info could have been a bit more easy, but otherwise it was simple.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered for my classes online through the UAB Barcelona website. The process was simple and straightforward, and the information about the available courses was easy to find.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help was available through the university’s international office and online information provided by UAB. The information was clear, and I was able to complete the registration process without any major issues

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful in registering for the classes I wanted. The online registration process was easy and I was able to register for my preferred courses without any major problems. Every class i wanted was made available for me. And that was perfect.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every teacher is different. So if you have to classes overlapping, dont worry. Explaining the situation to a teacher is very helpfull. And they will understand. But choose classes that are interresting and someting you could see yourself do.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
level was good in most classes. 

but one class: Semantics and pragmatics in spanish was way to difficult for an erasmus student. I falied the class alongside other students. Including native spanish speakers. The teacher was also very strict and none compasionate to my situation.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching in spain was more group work and active teaching with raising your hand and engaging rather than listening and seeing powerpoints

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: anthropology was fun, and something i would recomend for people. And everbody can take the course without it being to difficult.

questions.answer: from what i remember, there was no items that suprised me that much

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was almost an activity every single day at my dorm, and the ESN network also made it possible for every erasmus person to get out there and try some new things. The host institution also had flyers around and different events going events like foodmarkets, culture night and movie nights

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking, karaoke nights etc. Everything that is social with people abroad

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the city and the other citys of the host country. take train, fly or whatever. But explore the other parts

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. i felt like a week or two in the city i felt like home.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to events, say hi to people, never say no to an offer

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any differences challenging, more like interesting. So no challenge, just an adaptation

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: i really liked the food and the climate. The nature was also very different from back home. so that i liked a lot

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. apply for the dorm rooms quickly! they are high in demand
2. spend more time in the city and buy a T-jove card for transport
3. Join ESN events. Always fun and nice

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Besides the things that i have mentioned before then no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The connections i made, the memories and the overall experience and privellege i had to go to such a thing

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Probably balancing the work balance and having fun balance. Its tough trying to do both. 
The exmans were also difficult

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
